I am a PhD candidate at the University of Cambridge, in the department of History and Philosophy of Science. I am supervised by Dr. Hasok Chang and Dr. Marta Halina.

My main research areas are:

  • philosophy of experimentation,
  • pragmatist philosophy of science (esp. C.S. Peirce),
  • teleological explanations in science, and
  • philosophy of statistics.

I am a team member of “Using Material Models to Investigate Agency, Innovation, and Directionality in Evolution”, an international, interdisciplinary research project, led by C. Kenneth Waters.

Previously, I practised law at a global law firm in my hometown of Calgary, Alberta, Canada. I completed law school at Dalhousie University’s Schulich School of Law, and hold masters and undergraduate degrees in philosophy from the University of Calgary.

Please feel free to email me, or find me online at my department profile and on PhilPeople. Please also see my Teaching page, a copy of my CV, and my interactive illustrations.

Publications

  • Charles Peirce and Experimental Science. Transactions of the Charles S. Peirce Society, 61 (1):22–51 (2025).
    Winner of the 2024 Charles S. Peirce Society Essay Prize.
  • Learning by Trial and Error: The Roles for Purpose in Susan Haack’s Legal Pragmatism. Invited contribution, forthcoming.
  • Metatheoretical Linguistics: A Philosopher’s Guide. Biolinguistics (with Konstantinos Voudouris). An extended review of Nefdt, R., The Philosophy of Theoretical Linguistics.

Work in Progress

  • Various projects on the use of statistics in 19th Century experimentation.
  • A paper on Aristotle’s influence on Charles Peirce.
  • “Invisible Astronomy”, a paper on astronomical practices and philosophical questions related to the discovery of Neptune. With Janna Müller.
  • A paper on pursuitworthiness and artificial intelligence. With André Curtis-Trudel and Konstantinos Voudouris. Under review.
  • A paper on Noam Chomsky’s philosophy of science.
  • A review of Evolution ‘On Purpose’: Teleonomy in Living Systems.
